verses.1: To you, O LORD, I lift up my being.
verses.2: My God, in you I have trusted. Let me not be put to shame; let not my enemies rejoice over me.
verses.3: For all who wait for you shall not be put to shame; let the treacherous be put to shame through their emptiness.
verses.4: Make known to me your ways, O LORD, and teach me your paths.
verses.5: Guide me in your truth and teach me, for you are the God who is my salvation. In you I have waited all the day.
verses.6: Remember your mercies, O LORD, and your steadfast love, for they are from of old.
verses.7: Do not remember the sins of my youth and my transgressions. In your steadfast love, remember me, for your goodness is great, O LORD.
verses.8: The LORD is good and upright; therefore he teaches sinners the right way.
verses.9: He guides the humble in justice and teaches the humble his way.
verses.10: All the ways of the LORD are steadfast love and truth, to those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.
verses.11: For your name's sake, O LORD, forgive my iniquity, for it is great.
verses.12: Who is the man who fears the LORD? He will teach him the way he has chosen.
verses.13: His soul will rest in good things, and his descendants will inherit the land.
verses.14: The counsel of the LORD is for those who fear him, and his covenant is to make them know it.
verses.15: My eyes are always toward the LORD, for he will bring my feet out of the net.
verses.16: Turn your face toward me and be gracious to me, for I am alone and poor.
verses.17: The troubles of my heart are multiplied; bring me out from my distress.
verses.18: See my affliction and my toil, and forgive all my sins.
verses.19: See my enemies, for they are many, and they hate me with unjust hatred.
verses.20: Keep my soul and deliver me, let me not be put to shame, for I have trusted in you.
verses.21: The innocent and the upright have clung to me, because I have waited for you, O LORD.
verses.22: Rescue, O God, Israel from all his distress.

notes:
Notes
- v. 13: "His soul will rest in good things" — "rest" (תָּלִין) reflects a metaphor of hanging or leaning, here rendered as "rest" to capture the idea of finding peace in what is good.
- v. 14: "counsel of the LORD" — "סוֹד" (sod) often refers to a secret or intimate counsel. Here, it is rendered in a way that aligns with the context of divine revelation for those who fear the LORD.
- v. 21: "the innocent and the upright" — "תֹּם" (tom) and "יֹשֶׁר" (yosher) are translated as "innocent" and "upright" to reflect their moral qualities as described in the psalm.
